title.zh: 卷二百五十三 列傳第十二 折德扆 馮繼業 王承美 李繼周 孫行友
title.en: Volume 253 Biographies 12: Zhe Deyi, Feng Jiye, Wang Chengmei, Li Jizhou, Sun Xingyou
title.raw: 卷二百五十三 列傳第十二 折德扆 馮繼業 王承美 李繼周 孫行友 Volume 253 Biographies 12: Zhe Deyi, Feng Jiye, Wang Chengmei, Li Jizhou, Sun Xingyou

sentences.zh: 折德扆

translations.literal: Zhe Deyi
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Deyi

sentences.zh: 折德扆，世居雲中，為大族。

translations.literal: Zhe Deyi, whose family had long dwelt in Yunzhong, was a great clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Deyi came from a great clan that had long lived in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 父從阮，自晉、漢以來，獨據府州，控扼西北，中國賴之。

translations.literal: His father Congruan, since the Jin and Han dynasties, alone held Fuzhou, controlling and blocking the northwest; China relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhe Congruan had held Fuzhou alone since the Jin and Han periods, commanding the northwest frontier on which the Central Court depended.

sentences.zh: 仕周至靜難軍節度使。

translations.literal: He served Zhou and rose to Military Commissioner of the Jingnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he rose to become military commissioner of the Jingnan army.

sentences.zh: 其鎮府州時，署德扆為馬步軍都校。

translations.literal: When he governed Fuzhou, he appointed Deyi as commander-in-chief of the horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Fuzhou, he appointed Deyi commander of the combined horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 廣順間，周世宗建府州為永安軍，以德扆為節度使，時從阮鎮邠寧，父子俱領節鎮，時人榮之。

translations.literal: During the Guangshun era, Emperor Shizong of Zhou established Fuzhou as the Yong'an Army and made Deyi its military commissioner; at that time Congruan governed Binning, father and son both holding commanderies, and people of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangshun period Emperor Shizong of Zhou made Fuzhou the Yong'an army and appointed Deyi its military commissioner, while Congruan held Binning—father and son both commanding frontier circuits, to the envy of their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，德扆率師攻下河市鎮，斬幷軍五百餘級。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era, Deyi led troops to attack and take Hexiahe Town, beheading more than five hundred Bingzhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande reign Deyi led an assault that captured Hexiahe town and killed more than five hundred soldiers of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 入朝，以其弟德愿權總州事。

translations.literal: He entered court, and his younger brother Deyuan was appointed to oversee prefectural affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: He went to court and left his younger brother Deyuan in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時世宗南征，還次通許橋，德扆迎謁，且請遷內地。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Shizong was on a southern campaign and halted at Tongxu Bridge; Deyi came to meet him and also requested relocation to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was returning from his southern campaign and halted at Tongxu Bridge; Deyi came to pay his respects and asked to be moved inland.

sentences.zh: 世宗以其素得蕃情，不許，厚加賜賚而遣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because he had long won the hearts of the frontier peoples, did not permit it, but richly rewarded him and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, saying Deyi had long understood the frontier tribes, but sent him home with generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 德扆未至，德愿又破幷軍五百餘於沙谷砦，斬其將郝章、張釗。

translations.literal: Before Deyi arrived, Deyuan again defeated more than five hundred Bingzhou troops at Shagu Fort, beheading their generals Hao Zhang and Zhang Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Before Deyi returned, Deyuan routed another five hundred Bingzhou troops at Shagu fort and killed their generals Hao Zhang and Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子 御勳

translations.literal: Son: Yuxun
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yuxun

sentences.zh: 御勳，字世隆，德扆鎮府州日，表為右職。

translations.literal: Yuxun, style name Shilong, when Deyi governed Fuzhou, was recommended for a senior post on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxun, styled Shilong, was recommended for a senior staff post while his father governed Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 德扆卒，以御勳領汾州團練使、權知府州事。

translations.literal: When Deyi died, Yuxun was made regimental commander of Fenzhou and acting prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Deyi's death Yuxun was made regimental commander of Fenzhou and acting prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，太祖征太原，御勳詣行在謁見，以為永安軍留後。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, when the Taizu campaigned against Taiyuan, Yuxun went to the imperial camp to pay respects and was made acting commissioner of the Yong'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 969, when Taizu marched on Taiyuan, Yuxun came to the imperial camp and was appointed acting commissioner of the Yong'an army.

sentences.zh: 四年，以郊祀來朝，禮畢歸鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he came to court for the suburban sacrifice; when the rites were finished he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he came to court for the suburban sacrifice and returned to his post when the rites ended.

sentences.zh: 九年，郊祀西洛，復來朝，道病後期，改泰寧軍節度使，留京師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when the suburban sacrifice was held in western Luoyang, he came to court again; on the road he fell ill and arrived late, was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Taining Army, and remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 976 he came again for the suburban sacrifice at Luoyang, fell ill on the road and arrived late, was made military commissioner of the Taining army, and was kept at the capital.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，卒，年四十，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he died, aged forty, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 977 at the age of forty and was posthumously made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 子 御卿

translations.literal: Son: Yuqing
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yuqing

sentences.zh: 御卿，幼補節院使，御勳知州事，署為兵馬都校。

translations.literal: Yuqing, while young, was made an envoy of the military commission; when Yuxun governed the prefecture, he was appointed commander of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing entered service young as a military-commission envoy; when Yuxun governed the prefecture he was appointed commander of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 御勳徙鎮，召為閑廄副使、知府州。

translations.literal: When Yuxun was transferred to another command, Yuqing was summoned as Deputy Commissioner of the Imperial Stud and made prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuxun was transferred elsewhere, Yuqing was summoned as deputy commissioner of the imperial stud and made prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，命御卿與尹憲領屯兵同攻嵐州，又破岢嵐軍，擒其軍使折令圖以獻，遂下嵐州，又殺其憲州刺史霍翊，又擒其將馬延忠等七人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned in Hedong, he ordered Yuqing and Yin Xian to lead garrison troops together to attack Lanzhou; they also defeated the Kelan army, captured its army commander Zhe Lingtu and presented him, then took Lanzhou, also killed its Xianzhou prefect Huo Yi, and also captured its generals Ma Yanzhong and six others.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizong's Hedong campaign Yuqing and Yin Xian jointly led garrison troops against Lanzhou, routed the Kelan army, captured its commander Zhe Lingtu and presented him, took the city, killed Xianzhou prefect Huo Yi, and seized seven enemy generals including Ma Yanzhong.

sentences.zh: 遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of Honored Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commissioner of honored rites.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，凡四遷而為府州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, after four promotions in all, he became Observation Commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By the third year of Chunhua, after four promotions, he had become observation commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜永安軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Yong'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he was formally appointed military commissioner of the Yong'an army.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹眾萬餘入寇，御卿大敗之於子河氵義，斬首五千級，獲馬千匹，契丹將號突厥太尉、司徒、舍利死者二十餘人，擒其吐渾一人，自是契丹知所畏。

translations.literal: Soon after, more than ten thousand Khitan troops invaded; Yuqing routed them at Ziheyi, beheading five thousand, capturing a thousand horses; more than twenty Khitan officers titled Tujue Grand Commandant, Minister, and Sheli died, and one Tuhun was captured; from then on the Khitan knew whom to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward more than ten thousand Khitan invaded; Yuqing crushed them at Ziheyi, taking five thousand heads and a thousand horses, killing more than twenty Khitan officers bearing titles such as Tujue grand commandant, minister, and sheli, and capturing a Tuhun warrior—from then on the Khitan learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 太宗因遣使問御卿曰：「西北要害皆屯勁兵，戎人何自而至？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong therefore sent an envoy to ask Yuqing, saying: "All the strategic points of the northwest are garrisoned with strong troops—how could the barbarians come on their own?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent an envoy to ask Yuqing, "Every key point in the northwest is held by strong garrisons—how could the barbarians have gotten through on their own?"

sentences.zh: 」御卿對曰：「敵緣山峽小徑入，謀剽略。

translations.literal: " Yuqing replied: "The enemy came in by narrow paths through mountain passes, intending to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing answered, "They came in by narrow mountain paths intending to raid.

sentences.zh: 臣諜知之，遣人邀其歸路，因縱兵大擊，敗走之，人馬墜厓谷死者相忱，其大將韓德威僅以身免。

translations.literal: Your servant learned this through spies, sent men to block their line of retreat, then unleashed the army in a great attack and routed them; men and horses falling into ravines and gorges lay piled upon one another; their great general Han Dewei barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: I learned this through spies, blocked their retreat, and struck hard; men and horses fell into ravines in heaps, and their commander Han Dewei barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 皆聖靈所及，非臣之功也。

translations.literal: All this was reached by your sacred spirit—it is not your servant's merit."
translations.idiomatic: That was your sacred power at work, not mine."

sentences.zh: 」上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，御卿被病，德威諜知之，且為李繼遷所誘，率眾來侵，以報子河氵義之役。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Yuqing fell ill; Han Dewei learned this through spies and, moreover, being enticed by Li Jiqian, led a host to invade to avenge the battle at Ziheyi.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Yuqing fell ill; Han Dewei learned of it through spies and, urged on by Li Jiqian, led a force to invade and avenge Ziheyi.

sentences.zh: 御卿力疾出戰，德威聞其至，不敢進。

translations.literal: Yuqing forced himself out to battle though ill; when Han Dewei heard he had come, he did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing dragged himself into battle despite his illness; when Han Dewei heard he had come out, he did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 會疾甚，其母密遣人召歸，御卿曰：「世受國恩，邊寇未滅，御卿罪也。

translations.literal: When his illness grew severe, his mother secretly sent someone to summon him home; Yuqing said: "Our family has received the state's grace for generations; if border enemies are not destroyed, it is Yuqing's fault.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness worsened his mother secretly sent for him; Yuqing said, "Our family has owed the state for generations; if the border enemy is not destroyed, that is my fault.

sentences.zh: 今臨敵棄士卒自便，不可，死於軍中乃其分也。

translations.literal: Now to abandon the troops before the enemy for my own convenience cannot be done; to die in the army is one's proper lot."
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the troops now for my own comfort is impossible; dying in the ranks is my proper duty."

sentences.zh: 為白太夫人，無念我，忠孝豈兩全！

translations.literal: Tell the Lady Dowager for me: do not think of me—how can loyalty and filial piety both be fulfilled!"
translations.idiomatic: Tell my mother not to worry about me—loyalty and filial piety cannot both be satisfied!"

sentences.zh: 」言訖泣下。

translations.literal: When he had spoken, tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he finished speaking.

sentences.zh: 翌日卒，年三十八。

translations.literal: The next day he died, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next day, aged thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 上聞悼惜久之，贈侍中，以其子惟正為洛苑使、知州事。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he mourned and regretted for a long time, posthumously made him Palace Attendant, and appointed his son Weizheng as Commissioner of the Luoyang Park and to govern the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him at length, posthumously made him palace attendant, and appointed his son Weizheng commissioner of the Luoyang park and prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 惟正歸朝，以其弟惟昌繼之。

translations.literal: Weizheng returned to court, and his younger brother Weichang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Weizheng returned to court and his younger brother Weichang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，表求赴闕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he memorialized requesting to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1009 he petitioned to come to court.

sentences.zh: 真宗命近臣與射於苑中，宴賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong ordered close ministers to shoot with him in the park and gave him a very generous feast and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong had his close ministers shoot with him in the imperial park and entertained him with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 上言：「先臣御卿蒙賜旗三十竿以壯軍容，請別給賜。

translations.literal: He said to the throne: "My late father Yuqing received the gift of thirty banner poles to enhance the army's appearance; I request a separate grant."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "My late father Yuqing was granted thirty banner poles to dignify his troops; I ask for a grant of my own."

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 七年，命河東民運糧赴麟州，當出兵為援，惟昌力疾領步騎屯寧遠砦，冒風沙而行。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Hedong commoners were ordered to transport grain to Linzhou and troops were to be sent in support, Weichang, though gravely ill, led foot and horse to garrison Ningyuan Fort, marching through wind and sand.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later, when Hedong civilians were ordered to haul grain to Linzhou and troops were required as escort, Weichang, though seriously ill, led infantry and cavalry to Ningyuan fort through wind and sand.

sentences.zh: 時疾已亟，猶與賓佐宴飲，談笑自若焉。

translations.literal: Though his illness was already severe, he still feasted and drank with guests and staff, talking and laughing as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Though his illness was grave, he still feasted with his staff, talking and laughing as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 明日卒，年三十七。

translations.literal: The next day he died, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next day, aged thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 以其弟惟忠繼之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Weizhong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Weizhong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 惟忠，字藎臣，初以兄惟信戰沒，補西頭供奉官，擢閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Weizhong, style name Jinchen, at first because his elder brother Weixin died in battle, was made a Western Head Palace Attendant, then promoted to Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong, styled Jinchen, first entered service as a western-head palace attendant because his elder brother Weixin had died in battle, then was promoted to gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及惟昌卒，以惟忠為六宅使、知府州兼麟府路都巡檢使，領普州刺史；

translations.literal: When Weichang died, Weizhong was made Commissioner of the Six Residences, prefect of Fuzhou and overall inspector of the Lin-Fu circuit, and also held the post of Puzhou prefect;
translations.idiomatic: When Weichang died, Weizhong was made commissioner of the six residences, prefect of Fuzhou and overall inspector of the Lin-Fu circuit, and also served as prefect of Puzhou;

sentences.zh: 再遷左藏庫使，真拜嘉州刺史，改資州，進簡州團練使。

translations.literal: he was again transferred to Commissioner of the Left Treasury, formally appointed prefect of Jiazhou, transferred to Zizhou, and advanced to regimental commander of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: he was later made commissioner of the left treasury, formally appointed prefect of Jiazhou, transferred to Zizhou, and promoted to regimental commander of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 喪母，起復雲麾將軍，卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he was recalled from mourning as Cloud-Banner General and then died.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he was recalled from mourning as cloud-banner general and soon died.

sentences.zh: 惟忠知兵事。

translations.literal: Weizhong understood military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong was skilled in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，契丹與夏國會兵境上，聲言嫁娶，惟忠覘得其實，率麾下往備之，戒士卒毋輕動。

translations.literal: During the Tiansheng era, Khitan and Xia joined forces on the border, claiming a marriage alliance; Weizhong reconnoitered and learned the truth, led his subordinates to prepare against them, and warned the troops not to act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng reign the Khitan and Xia massed on the border under the pretense of a marriage alliance; Weizhong discovered their real intent, led his men to prepare, and ordered the troops not to stir rashly.

sentences.zh: 一夕風霾，有騎走營中，以為寇至，惟忠堅臥不動，徐命擒之，得數誕馬，蓋虜所縱也。

translations.literal: One night in wind and haze, horsemen ran into the camp and were thought to be the enemy arriving; Weizhong lay firm and did not move, then slowly ordered them seized and obtained several stray horses—it turned out the barbarians had released them.
translations.idiomatic: One night in a sandstorm riders dashed into camp and were taken for the enemy; Weizhong stayed in bed unmoved, then calmly ordered them caught—they proved to be stray horses the barbarians had turned loose.

sentences.zh: 既卒，錄其弟侄子孫七人，以其子繼宣嗣州事。

translations.literal: After he died, seven younger brothers, nephews, and grandsons were enrolled in office, and his son Jixuan succeeded to prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After his death seven younger kinsmen were enrolled in office and his son Jixuan succeeded him as prefect.

sentences.zh: 久之，特贈惟忠耀州觀察使。

translations.literal: After a long time, Weizhong was specially posthumously made Observation Commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Weizhong was posthumously made observation commissioner of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 寶元中，繼宣坐苛虐掊刻，種落嗟怨，絀為左監門衛將軍、楚州都監，擢其弟右侍禁繼閔為西京作坊使，嗣州事。

translations.literal: During the Baoyuan era, Jixuan was demoted for cruelty and extortion that made the tribes lament and resent; he was reduced to Left Gate Guard General and superintendent of Chuzhou, and his younger brother, Right Palace Guard Jimin, was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and succeeded to prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoyuan period Jixuan was demoted for harsh extortion that angered the tribes; he was made left gate guard general and superintendent of Chuzhou, while his younger brother Jimin, a right palace guard, was promoted to commissioner of the western capital workshops and succeeded him at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 繼閔，字廣孝。

translations.literal: Jimin, style name Guangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Jimin, styled Guangxiao.

sentences.zh: 慶歷中，元昊兵攻麟州不克，進圍州城。

translations.literal: During the Qingli era, Yuan Hao's troops attacked Linzhou without success and advanced to besiege the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli reign Yuan Hao's army failed to take Linzhou and turned to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 城險且堅，東南有水門，厓壁峭絕，阻河。

translations.literal: The city was perilous and firm; to the southeast was a water gate, with cliff walls sheer and impassable, blocked by the river.
translations.idiomatic: The city was strong and perilous; on the southeast was a water gate where sheer cliffs dropped to the river.

sentences.zh: 賊緣厓腹微徑魚貫而前，城中矢石亂下，賊轉攻城北，士卒復力戰，賊死傷甚眾，遂引去，圍豐州，豐州遂陷。

translations.literal: The enemy climbed a narrow path along the cliff belly in single file; arrows and stones rained down from the city; the enemy turned to attack the north of the city, the troops fought again with force, the enemy dead and wounded were very many, and they then withdrew, besieged Fengzhou, and Fengzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy filed along a narrow cliff path; the defenders rained arrows and stones upon them; when the enemy shifted to the north wall the garrison fought them off again with heavy losses; the enemy withdrew, besieged Fengzhou, and Fengzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 繼閔以城守勞，特遷宮苑使、普州刺史。

translations.literal: Jimin, for his labor in defending the city, was specially promoted to Commissioner of the Imperial Park and prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his defense of the city Jimin was specially promoted to commissioner of the imperial park and prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，護送麟州戍卒冬服，賊伏兵邀擊之，盡掠所賫，繼閔脫身繇間道歸。

translations.literal: Before long, while escorting winter clothing for Linzhou garrison troops, the enemy ambushed them and plundered all they carried; Jimin escaped and returned by a hidden path.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, while escorting winter uniforms for the Linzhou garrison, he was ambushed and everything was seized; Jimin escaped by a back trail.

sentences.zh: 會赦，止奪宮苑使，後復官，領果州團練使。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was proclaimed, only his post as Commissioner of the Imperial Park was taken; later his office was restored and he held the regimental command of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared him further punishment beyond loss of the imperial-park commission; he was later restored and made regimental commander of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 自元昊反，繼閔招輯歸業者三千餘戶。

translations.literal: Since Yuan Hao rebelled, Jimin gathered and settled more than three thousand households returning to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao's rebellion Jimin resettled more than three thousand households who had fled.

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年，卒，以其弟繼祖嗣州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangyou he died, and his younger brother Jizu succeeded to prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1050 and his younger brother Jizu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 繼祖，字應之，由右侍禁遷西染院使，累轉皇城使、成州團練使。

translations.literal: Jizu, style name Yingzhi, rose from Right Palace Guard to Commissioner of the Western Dyeing Bureau, and through successive promotions became Imperial City Commissioner and regimental commander of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu, styled Yingzhi, rose from right palace guard to commissioner of the western dyeing bureau and through successive promotions became imperial city commissioner and regimental commander of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨政二十餘年。

translations.literal: He governed for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the prefecture for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 奏乞書籍，仁宗賜以《九經》。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting books; Emperor Renzong granted him the 《Nine Classics》.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for books and Renzong granted him the 《Nine Classics》.

sentences.zh: 韓絳發河東兵城囉兀，繼祖為先鋒，深入敵帳，降部落戶八百。

translations.literal: Han Jiang mobilized Hedong troops to fortify Lawu; Jizu served as vanguard, penetrated deep into the enemy encampment, and induced eight hundred tribal households to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang sent Hedong troops to build Lawu fort, Jizu led the vanguard, penetrated deep into enemy territory, and brought eight hundred tribal households to submit.

sentences.zh: 加解州防禦使，卒。

translations.literal: He was further made Defense Commissioner of Jiezhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to defense commissioner of Jiezhou and died.

sentences.zh: 繼祖有子當襲州事，請以授兄之子克柔，詔從之，而進其三子官，錄二孫為借職。

translations.literal: Jizu had a son who should have inherited prefectural affairs; he requested that it be given to his elder brother's son Kerou; an edict followed this, while his three sons were advanced in office and two grandsons were enrolled as borrowed posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu's son was heir to the prefecture, but he asked that it go to his elder brother's son Kerou; the court agreed, promoted his three sons, and enrolled two grandsons in office.

sentences.zh: 弟繼世，少從軍，為延州東路巡檢。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jishi, who joined the army young, was Eastern Route Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jishi entered the army young and became eastern-route inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嵬名山之內附，繼世先知之，遣其子克懃報种諤，諤用是取綏州。

translations.literal: When Wei Mingshan submitted to the court, Jishi knew it first, sent his son Keqin to report to Zhong E, and E thereby took Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Mingshan defected, Jishi learned of it first and sent his son Keqin to inform Zhong E, who thereby captured Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 繼世以騎步萬軍於懷寧砦，入晉祠谷，往銀川，分名山之眾萬五千戶居於大理河。

translations.literal: Jishi led ten thousand horse and foot at Huaining Fort, entered Jinci Valley, went to Yinchuan, and settled fifteen thousand households of Mingshan's followers along the Dali River.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi led ten thousand horse and foot from Huaining fort into Jinci valley and on to Yinchuan, resettling fifteen thousand of Mingshan's followers along the Dali River.

sentences.zh: 夏人來攻，再戰皆捷。

translations.literal: When Xia troops came to attack, he fought twice and won both times.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia attacked he fought twice and won both engagements.

sentences.zh: 諤抵罪逮繫獄，以兵付之而行，遂同名山守綏州，綠功領忠州刺史。

translations.literal: When E was punished and imprisoned, troops were entrusted to Jishi and he set out; he then guarded Suizhou together with Mingshan and, for his merit, held the prefecture of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong E was imprisoned for his crimes, Jishi was given his troops and marched out; he then held Suizhou with Mingshan and, for his service, was made prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 說韓絳城囉兀以撫橫山，因畫取河南之策，絳以為然。

translations.literal: He persuaded Han Jiang to fortify Lawu in order to pacify Hengshan, and thereby outlined a plan to take the lands south of the river; Jiang approved.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded Han Jiang to build Lawu to pacify Hengshan and sketched a plan to seize the territory south of the Yellow River; Jiang agreed.

sentences.zh: 以左騏驥使、果州團練使卒。

translations.literal: He died while holding the posts of Left Commissioner of Fine Horses and regimental commander of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as left commissioner of fine horses and regimental commander of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 諸司使無賻禮，詔以繼世蕃官，捍邊有績，特給之。

translations.literal: Commissioners of the various bureaus were not given funeral gifts; an edict stated that because Jishi was a frontier tribal official who had defended the border with achievement, it was specially granted.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioners normally received no funeral gifts, but the court ruled that as a frontier tribal officer who had distinguished himself on the border, Jishi should receive them.

sentences.zh: 從子克行。

translations.literal: Nephew: Kexing
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Kexing

sentences.zh: 曾孫 克行

translations.literal: Great-grandson: Kexing
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson: Kexing

sentences.zh: 克行，字遵道，繼閔子也。

translations.literal: Kexing, style name Zundao, was Jimin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Kexing, styled Zundao, was Jimin's son.

sentences.zh: 初仕軍府，無所知名。

translations.literal: At first he served in the military prefecture and was not known for anything.
translations.idiomatic: He first served in the military prefecture without distinction.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇環慶，种諤拒之，詔河東出師為援，克行請往。

translations.literal: When Xia troops raided Huanqing, Zhong E resisted them; an edict ordered Hedong to send troops in support, and Kexing requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia raided Huanqing, Zhong E held them off; the court ordered Hedong to reinforce him, and Kexing volunteered.

sentences.zh: 諤使以兵三千護餉道，戰於葭蘆川，先登，斬級四百，降戶千，馬畜萬計。

translations.literal: E sent him with three thousand troops to guard the supply route; they fought at Jialu River, Kexing climbed first, beheaded four hundred, induced a thousand households to submit, and took tens of thousands of horses and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong E sent him with three thousand men to guard the supply line; at Jialu River Kexing was first up the wall, took four hundred heads, brought a thousand households to submit, and captured tens of thousands of horses and livestock.

sentences.zh: 諸老將矍然曰：「真折太尉子也！

translations.literal: The veteran generals started in astonishment and said: "Truly a son of Grand Marshal Zhe!"
translations.idiomatic: The veteran generals exclaimed, "A true son of Grand Marshal Zhe!"

sentences.zh: 」擢知府州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to govern Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦兵討夏國，張世矩將河外軍民，克行與俱。

translations.literal: Qin troops campaigned against the Xia state; Zhang Shiju led the army and people beyond the river, and Kexing went with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin forces campaigned against Xia, Zhang Shiju led the troops and civilians beyond the river, and Kexing went with him.

sentences.zh: 廷議謂守臣難自行，詔克行選兵隸世矩。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that frontier defenders could hardly act on their own; an edict ordered Kexing to select troops and place them under Shiju.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that border commanders could not march on their own; Kexing was ordered to select troops and place them under Zhang Shiju.

sentences.zh: 克行抗章，願率部落先驅，未報，即委管鑰而西。

translations.literal: Kexing submitted a memorial in opposition, wishing to lead his tribes as vanguard; before a reply came, he entrusted the keys of office and marched west.
translations.idiomatic: Kexing protested in a memorial that he wished to lead his tribes as vanguard; before a reply arrived he handed over his keys and marched west.

sentences.zh: 大酋咩保吳良以萬騎來躡，克行為後拒，度賊半度隘，縱擊大破之，殺咩保吳良。

translations.literal: The great chieftain Miebao Wuliang came with ten thousand horsemen in pursuit; Kexing served as rear guard, judged when half the enemy had passed the defile, then unleashed an attack and routed them greatly, killing Miebao Wuliang.
translations.idiomatic: The great chieftain Miebao Wuliang pursued with ten thousand horsemen; Kexing covered the rear, waited until half the enemy had passed the defile, then struck and routed them, killing Miebao Wuliang.

sentences.zh: 師還自劾，釋不問。

translations.literal: When the army returned he impeached himself, but was released without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he submitted a self-impeachment, but the court took no action.

sentences.zh: 王中正出塞，克行先拔宥州，每出必勝，夏人畏之，益左廂兵，專以當折氏。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhongzheng went beyond the frontier, Kexing first took Youzhou; every time he went out he was sure to win; the Xia feared him and increased the left wing army specifically to oppose the Zhe clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhongzheng campaigned beyond the frontier, Kexing first captured Youzhou; he never marched without victory; the Xia feared him and reinforced their left wing specifically to face the Zhe family.

sentences.zh: 太原孫覽議城葭蘆，諸將論多不合，召克行問策，即頓兵吐渾河，約勒部伍，為深入窮討之狀，敵疑不敢動。

translations.literal: Sun Lan of Taiyuan proposed fortifying Jialu; the generals' discussions mostly disagreed, so Kexing was summoned to ask his plan; he at once halted troops at the Tuhun River, disciplined his units, and made a show of deep pursuit to the end, so the enemy suspected and did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lan of Taiyuan proposed building a fort at Jialu; when the generals could not agree, Kexing was consulted; he halted at the Tuhun River, drilled his men, and feigned a deep pursuit so the enemy dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 既訖役，又入津慶、龍橫川，斬級三千。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he again entered Jinqing and Longhengchuan and beheaded three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the fort was finished he raided Jinqing and Longhengchuan and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 詔河東進築八砦，通道鄜延。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hedong to advance and build eight forts, opening a route to Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Hedong to build eight advance forts and open a route to Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 延帥遣秦希甫來共議，克行請兩路併力，以遠者為先，希甫曰：「由近及遠，法也。

translations.literal: The Fuyan commander sent Qin Xifu to discuss together; Kexing requested that both routes combine strength and take the distant first; Xifu said: "From near to far—that is the rule."
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyan commander sent Qin Xifu to consult; Kexing urged both circuits to combine forces and begin with the farthest posts; Xifu said, "From near to far—that is the rule."

sentences.zh: 」克行曰：「不然，事有奇正。

translations.literal: " Kexing said: "Not so—affairs have orthodox and unorthodox methods."
translations.idiomatic: Kexing replied, "Not so—there are orthodox and unorthodox ways to war."

sentences.zh: 今乘士氣之銳，所利在速，故先遠役，以出其不意，若徐圖之，士心且怠矣。

translations.literal: Now, riding the sharpness of troop morale, what profits us is speed; therefore work the distant posts first to take them unawares—if we proceed slowly, the soldiers' hearts will slacken."
translations.idiomatic: Morale is high and speed is everything—we must build the distant forts first and catch them unawares; delay will only dull the men's spirit."

sentences.zh: 」希甫持不可，並上二議，卒用克行策。

translations.literal: Xifu held that it could not be done; both plans were submitted together, and in the end Kexing's plan was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Xifu objected; both plans went up to the throne, and Kexing's was adopted.

sentences.zh: 城成，諜言寇至，軍中皆戒嚴，克行止之曰：「彼自擾耳。

translations.literal: When the fort was completed, spies reported that the enemy had arrived; the whole army went on alert; Kexing stopped them and said: "They are frightening themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When the fort was finished, scouts reported the enemy was coming and the army went on alert; Kexing stopped them. "They are only frightening themselves," he said.

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enough it proved true.

sentences.zh: 克行在邊三十年，善拊士卒，戰功最多，羌人呼為『折家父』。

translations.literal: Kexing was on the frontier for thirty years, good at comforting the troops; his battle achievements were the greatest; the Qiang called him "Father of the Zhe Family."
translations.idiomatic: Kexing served on the frontier for thirty years, won the soldiers' loyalty, and amassed more victories than any other; the Qiang called him "Father Zhe."

sentences.zh: 官至秦州觀察使，卒，贈武安軍節度使。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Observation Commissioner of Qinzhou, died, and was posthumously made Military Commissioner of the Wu'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to observation commissioner of Qinzhou, died, and was posthumously made military commissioner of the Wu'an army.

sentences.zh: 子可大為榮州團練使、知府州。

translations.literal: His son Kedai was made regimental commander of Rongzhou and prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kedai became regimental commander of Rongzhou and prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 從子可適。

translations.literal: Nephew: Keshi.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Keshi.

sentences.zh: 可適未冠有勇，馳射不習而能。

translations.literal: Keshi, before his capping, was brave; in mounted archery he could do it without study.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age Keshi was already brave and a natural horseman and archer.

sentences.zh: 鄜延郭逵見之，歎曰：「真將種也！

translations.literal: Guo Kui of Fuyan saw him and sighed: "Truly born of a general's stock!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Kui of Fuyan saw him and exclaimed, "A true soldier's breed!"

sentences.zh: 」薦試廷中，補殿侍，隸延州。

translations.literal: He was recommended for examination at court, made a palace attendant, and attached to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended for court examination, made a palace attendant, and assigned to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 從种諤出塞，遇敵馬以少年易之，可適索與鬥，斬其首，取馬而還，益知名，米脂之役，與夏人戰三角嶺，得級多，又敗之於蒲桃谷東。

translations.literal: Following Zhong E beyond the frontier, he met enemy horsemen who belittled him for his youth; Keshi demanded to fight, beheaded one, took his horse and returned, and became still better known; in the Mizhi campaign he fought the Xia at Sanjiao Ridge and took many heads, and again defeated them east of Putao Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning beyond the frontier with Zhong E, he met enemy riders who mocked his youth; Keshi insisted on a duel, cut off a head, seized the horse, and returned to greater fame; at Mizhi he fought the Xia at Sanjiao Ridge with many kills and routed them again east of Putao Valley.

sentences.zh: 兵久不得食，千人成聚，籍籍於軍門，或欲掩殺以為功，可適曰：「此以饑而逃耳，非叛也。

translations.literal: The troops had long gone without food; a thousand men gathered and murmured at the army gate; some wished to slaughter them secretly for merit; Keshi said: "These flee from hunger—it is not rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: After long hunger a thousand men gathered murmuring at headquarters; some wanted to slaughter them for credit; Keshi said, "They are running from hunger, not rebelling."

sentences.zh: 」單馬出詰之曰：「爾輩何至是，不為父母妻子念而甘心為異域鬼耶？

translations.literal: He went out alone on horseback to question them: "Why have you come to this? Will you not think of parents, wives, and children, but willingly become ghosts in a foreign land?"
translations.idiomatic: He rode out alone and demanded, "How can you do this—forget your parents, wives, and children and choose to die as ghosts in enemy country?"

sentences.zh: 」皆回面聲喏，流涕謝再生，各遣歸。

translations.literal: They all turned their faces, shouted assent, wept and thanked him for renewed life, and were each sent home.
translations.idiomatic: They turned, shouted assent, wept their thanks for new life, and were sent home one by one.

sentences.zh: 羌、夏人十萬入寇，可適先得其守烽卒姓名，詐為首領行視，呼出塞斬之，烽不傳，因卷甲疾趨，大破之於尾丁磑。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand Qiang and Xia invaded; Keshi first obtained the names of the beacon guards, pretended to be a chieftain on inspection, called them out beyond the pass and beheaded them so beacons were not passed; then he rolled up armor and hurried, routing them greatly at Weiding'ao.
translations.idiomatic: When a hundred thousand Qiang and Xia invaded, Keshi learned the beacon guards' names, posed as a chieftain on inspection, lured them beyond the pass and killed them before alarms could spread, then marched swiftly and crushed the enemy at Weiding'ao.

sentences.zh: 回次檉楊溝，正午駐營，分騎據西山，曰：「彼若躡吾後，腹背受敵，必敗。

translations.literal: On the return he halted at Chenyang Gully; at noon he camped, divided cavalry to hold the western hills, and said: "If they follow our rear, we will be attacked front and back and surely be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: On the march back he camped at Chenyang Gully at noon, posted cavalry on the western hills, and said, "If they follow us we will be caught between two fires and surely lose."

sentences.zh: 」果舉軍來，可適所部𦆵八千，轉戰至高嶺，廼從間道趣洪德，設伏邀其歸路。

translations.literal: The enemy did indeed bring their whole army; Keshi's command was only eight thousand; he fought in retreat to Gaoling, then took a hidden path toward Hongde and set an ambush on their line of return.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came in full force; with only eight thousand men Keshi fought his way to Gaoling, then took a back trail to Hongde and laid an ambush on their retreat.

sentences.zh: 敵至，伏發衝之，其國母窬山而遁，焚棄輜重，雖帷賬首飾之屬亦不返，眾相蹈藉，赴厓澗死者如積。

translations.literal: When the enemy arrived, the ambush sprang and charged them; their queen mother fled over the mountains; they burned and abandoned baggage; even curtains, tents, and head ornaments were not taken back; the masses trampled one another; those who fell into cliffs and ravines died in heaps.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrived the ambush struck; their queen mother fled over the mountains; they abandoned and burned their baggage, leaving even tents and ornaments behind; the rout trampled the dead in heaps in the ravines.

sentences.zh: 論前後功，至皇城使、成州團練使、知岷蘭州鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: Considering his achievements before and after, he rose to Imperial City Commissioner, regimental commander of Chengzhou, and administrator of Minzhou, Lanzhou, and Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: For his cumulative service he was made imperial city commissioner, regimental commander of Chengzhou, and administrator of Minzhou, Lanzhou, and the Zhenrong army.

sentences.zh: 渭帥章楶合熙、秦、慶三道兵築好水川，命總管王文振統之，而可適將軍為副。

translations.literal: Zhang Jie, commander of Wei, combined troops of the Xi, Qin, and Qing circuits to build Haoshui River fort; he ordered overall commander Wang Wenzhen to command them, with General Keshi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie of Wei combined the Xi, Qin, and Qing circuits to fortify Haoshui River and put Wang Wenzhen in overall command with Keshi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 熙州兵千人失道盡死，文振歸罪於可適，楶即下之吏，宰相章惇欲按軍法，哲宗不許，猶削十三官而罷。

translations.literal: A thousand Xi troops lost their way and all died; Wenzhen blamed Keshi; Jie at once handed him to the officials; Chancellor Zhang Dun wished to punish by military law; Emperor Zhezong did not permit it, but still stripped thirteen ranks and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When a thousand Xi troops lost their way and perished, Wenzhen blamed Keshi; Jie had him arrested; Chancellor Zhang Dun wanted a court-martial; Zhezong refused but still stripped thirteen ranks and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 楶請留以責效，乃以權第十二將。

translations.literal: Jie requested that he be kept to answer with achievement, and he was made acting Twelfth General.
translations.idiomatic: Jie asked to keep him on to redeem himself, and he was made acting commander of the twelfth division.

sentences.zh: 嵬名阿埋、昧勒都逋，皆夏人桀黠用事者，詔可適密圖之，會二酋以畜牧為名會境上，可適諜知之，遣兵夜往襲，並俘其族屬三千人，遂取天都山。

translations.literal: Weiming Ami and Mile Dubo were both fierce and cunning Xia men in power; an edict ordered Keshi to plot against them secretly; the two chiefs met on the border in the name of herding livestock; Keshi learned this through spies, sent troops by night to raid, and together captured three thousand of their clansmen, then took Tiandu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Weiming Ami and Mile Dubo were powerful, cunning Xia leaders; the court ordered Keshi to eliminate them; when the two chiefs met on the border ostensibly to graze livestock, Keshi learned of it, struck by night, captured three thousand of their kin, and seized Tiandu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝為御文德殿受賀，以其地為西安州，遷可適東上閤門使、洺州防禦使、涇原鈐轄、知州事，真拜和州防禦使，進明州觀察使，為副都總管。

translations.literal: The emperor received congratulations in the Wende Hall; that territory was made Xi'anzhou; Keshi was transferred to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, Defense Commissioner of Mingzhou, Jingyuan Commandant, and prefect; formally appointed Defense Commissioner of Hezhou; advanced to Observation Commissioner of Mingzhou; and made Deputy Overall Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received congratulations in the Wende Hall; the territory became Xi'anzhou; Keshi was made eastern upper gate commissioner, defense commissioner of Mingzhou, Jingyuan commandant and prefect, then formally defense commissioner of Hezhou, observation commissioner of Mingzhou, and deputy overall commander.

sentences.zh: 帥鐘傳行邊，為敵所隔，以輕騎拔之，得歸。

translations.literal: Commander Zhong Chuan was touring the border and was cut off by the enemy; Keshi with light cavalry rescued him and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander Zhong Chuan was cut off on the border, Keshi broke through with light cavalry and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 傳議取靈武，環慶，亦請出師，命可適將萬騎往，即薄靈州川。

translations.literal: Chuan discussed taking Lingwu and Huanqing and also requested to send troops; Keshi was ordered to lead ten thousand horsemen thither and at once pressed close to Lingzhou River.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan proposed taking Lingwu and Huanqing and asked for troops; Keshi was ordered to lead ten thousand cavalry and advanced to the Lingzhou River.

sentences.zh: 夏人扶老挾稚，中夜入州城，明日俘獲甚夥，而慶兵不至，乃引還。

translations.literal: The Xia, supporting the old and leading the young, entered the prefectural city at midnight; the next day captives were very many, but Qing troops did not arrive, so he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia, old and young together, entered the city at midnight; by morning the captures were immense, but Qing reinforcements never came, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔使人覲，帝以傳策訪焉，對曰：「得之易，守之難，當先侵弱其地，待吾藩籬既固，然後可圖。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him to audience; the emperor consulted him on Chuan's plan and he replied: "Taking it is easy, holding it hard; we should first invade and weaken their territory, wait until our frontier barriers are firm, and only then can we plan further."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was asked about Chuan's plan and answered, "It is easy to take but hard to hold—we should first raid and weaken their territory, secure our frontier defenses, and only then press further."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 」進武安軍節度觀察留後、步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of the Wu'an Army and Overall Adjutant of the Foot Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting military and observation commissioner of the Wu'an army and overall adjutant of the foot army.

sentences.zh: 大城蕭關，與傳議齟齬，會覆師數百於踏口，傳劾之，貶鄭州觀察使。

translations.literal: He greatly fortified Xiaoguan, clashed with Chuan in counsel, and when several hundred troops were lost at Tako, Chuan impeached him and he was demoted to Observation Commissioner of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Xiaoguan on a large scale, quarreled with Chuan, and when several hundred men were lost at Tako, Chuan impeached him and he was demoted to observation commissioner of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄知衛州，拜淮康軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he governed Weizhou and was appointed Military Commissioner of the Huaikang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Weizhou and military commissioner of the Huaikang army.

sentences.zh: 轉運使請於平夏、通峽、鎮戎、西安四砦分築場圃，置芻粟五百萬，可適以費大難之，又欲借車牛以運，及致十萬斛於熙河，皆戾其意，乃中以疑謗，召為佑神觀使。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner requested that at the four forts of Pingxia, Tongxia, Zhenrong, and Xi'an separate fields and pens be built and five million units of fodder and grain stored; Keshi objected that the expense was too great; he also wished to borrow carts and oxen for transport and to deliver a hundred thousand hu to Xihe—all contrary to the commissioner's intent; he was then impeached on suspicion of slander and summoned as Commissioner of the Youshen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner wanted to build granaries at four frontier forts and stock five million units of fodder; Keshi protested the cost, sought carts and oxen to haul grain, and planned to move a hundred thousand hu to Xihe—all against the commissioner's wishes; he was accused of obstruction and recalled as commissioner of the Youshen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以為渭州，命其子彥質直秘閣參軍事，數月而卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: The next year he was again made prefect of Weizhou; his son Yanzhi was ordered as Direct Secretariat Archives Participating Administrator; within several months he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again made prefect of Weizhou; his son Yanzhi was made a direct secretariat archives administrator; he died several months later at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 彥質，紹興中簽書樞密院，別有傳。

translations.literal: Yanzhi, in the Shaoxing era, signed documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi later signed documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs in the Shaoxing era; his biography is given elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 馮繼業

translations.literal: Feng Jiye
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jiye

sentences.zh: 馮繼業，字嗣宗，大名人。

translations.literal: Feng Jiye, style name Sizong, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jiye, styled Sizong, was from Daming.

sentences.zh: 父暉，朔方節度，封衛王。

translations.literal: His father Hui was Military Commissioner of Shuofang and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was military commissioner of Shuofang and was enfeoffed as prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 繼業幼敏慧，有度量，以父任補朔方軍節院使，隨父歷邠、孟，及再領朔方，皆補牙職。

translations.literal: Jiye in youth was clever and had breadth of mind; through his father's position he was made envoy of the Shuofang military commission; he followed his father through Bin and Meng, and when he again led Shuofang, he was each time given a staff post.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and broad-minded as a youth, Jiye entered service through his father as envoy of the Shuofang commission, followed him through Bin and Meng, and whenever his father again held Shuofang received a staff appointment.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，暉疾，繼業圖殺其兄繼勳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou's Guangshun era, when Hui fell ill, Jiye plotted to kill his elder brother Jixun.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun period, when Hui fell ill, Jiye plotted to kill his elder brother Jixun.

sentences.zh: 暉卒，遂代其父為朔方軍留後。

translations.literal: When Hui died, he then replaced his father as Acting Commissioner of the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died he succeeded his father as acting commissioner of the Shuofang army.

sentences.zh: 以郊祀恩，加靈州大都督府長史，遷朔方節度、靈環觀察、處置、度支、溫池榷稅等使。

translations.literal: Through the suburban-sacrifice grace, he was made Chief Secretary of the Lingzhou Grand Protectorate, and transferred to Military Commissioner of Shuofang, Observation Commissioner of Ling and Huan, Disposition, Revenue, and Wenchi Monopoly Tax Commissioner, and other posts.
translations.idiomatic: By suburban-sacrifice grace he was made chief secretary of the Lingzhou grand protectorate and military commissioner of Shuofang with concurrent posts over Ling and Huan, disposition, revenue, and the Wenchi salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 恭帝時，繼業既殺兄代父領鎮，頗驕恣，時出兵劫略羌夷，羌夷不附，又撫士卒少恩，繼業慮其為變，以太祖居鎮日常得給事，乃豫徙其孥闕下。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gong, Jiye, having killed his brother and replaced his father in command of the circuit, was quite arrogant and willful; he often sent troops to raid Qiang and Yi peoples; the Qiang and Yi would not submit; he also showed the troops little kindness; Jiye feared they would mutiny; because the Taizu when he was in the circuit had often been able to attend on him, he beforehand moved his women and children to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gong, Jiye had killed his brother and taken his father's command; arrogant and overbearing, he raided the Qiang and Yi until they would not submit and showed his troops little kindness; fearing mutiny, and remembering how Taizu had once served in the circuit, he moved his family to the capital in advance.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，來朝，連以駝馬、寶器為獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong he came to court and repeatedly presented camels, horses, and precious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianlong he came to court bearing camels, horses, and precious goods.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，賜詔獎諭，拜靜難軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, an edict was granted praising and instructing him, and he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Jingnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 969 an edict praised him and he was made military commissioner of the Jingnan army.

sentences.zh: 三年，改鎮定國軍，吏民立碑頌其遺愛。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to the Dingguo Army; officials and people erected a stele praising his lingering kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to the Dingguo army, and the people erected a stele praising his benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初來朝，封梁國公，留京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he came to court, was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang, and remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he came to court, was made duke of Liang, and was kept at the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，年五十一，贈侍中。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged fifty-one, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year at fifty-one and was posthumously made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 王承美

translations.literal: Wang Chengmei
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengmei

sentences.zh: 王承美，豐州人，本河西藏才族都首領。

translations.literal: Wang Chengmei, a native of Fengzhou, was originally chief of all the Zangcai tribe of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengmei of Fengzhou was originally chief of the Zangcai tribe of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 其父事契丹，為左千牛衛將軍，開寶二年，率眾來歸。

translations.literal: His father served the Khitan as Left Imperial Guard General; in the second year of Kaibao he led his followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His father had served the Khitan as left imperial guard general; in 969 he led his people to defect.

sentences.zh: 承美授豐州牙內指揮使，父卒，改天德軍蕃漢都指揮使、知州事，移豐州刺史。

translations.literal: Chengmei was appointed Fengzhou Inner Garrison Commander; when his father died, he was changed to Tiande Army Overall Tribal-and-Han Commander and prefect, then transferred to Fengzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmei was made Fengzhou inner garrison commander; after his father's death he became overall tribal-and-Han commander of the Tiande army and prefect, then Fengzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 遣軍校詣闕，言願誘退渾、突厥內附，上嘉其意。

translations.literal: He sent a military officer to court saying he wished to entice the Hun and Tujue to withdraw and submit inward; the emperor praised his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an officer to court offering to lure the Hun and Turks to submit; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 太平興國七年，與契丹戰，斬獲以萬計，禽其天德軍節度使韋太以獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo he fought the Khitan; kills and captures were counted by tens of thousands; he captured their Tiande Army Military Commissioner Wei Tai and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: In 982 he fought the Khitan, killing and capturing by the tens of thousands, and presented their Tiande army commander Wei Tai as a captive.

sentences.zh: 明年，契丹來寇，又擊敗其眾萬餘，追北至青冢百餘里，斬獲益眾。

translations.literal: The next year the Khitan invaded; he again defeated more than ten thousand of their host, pursued north to Qingzhong for more than a hundred li, and kills and captures were still greater.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he repelled a Khitan invasion, routed more than ten thousand of them, and pursued north to Qingzhong for over a hundred li with still greater slaughter.

sentences.zh: 以功授本州團練使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed regimental commander of his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made regimental commander of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以乞黨族次首領弗香克浪買為歸德郎將，沒細大首領越移為懷化大將軍，瓦窯為歸德大將軍。

translations.literal: The Qidang tribe's secondary chieftain Fuxiangkelangmai was made Returning Virtue Commandant; the Mosi great chieftain Yueyi was made Cherishing Transformation Grand General; Wayao was made Returning Virtue Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He made the Qidang secondary chief Fuxiangkelangmai a returning-virtue commandant, the Mosi great chief Yueyi a cherishing-transformation grand general, and Wayao a returning-virtue grand general.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年冬來朝，令歸所部，控子河�。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Chunhua he came to court; he was ordered to return to his command and control Ziheyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 991 he came to court and was sent back to his command to hold Ziheyi.

sentences.zh: 自是諸蕃歲修貢禮，頗效忠順。

translations.literal: From then on the various tribes yearly observed tribute rites and largely showed loyalty and submission.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the tribes paid annual tribute and showed marked loyalty.

sentences.zh: 景德初來朝，以其守邊歲久，遷本州防禦使以還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he came to court; because he had long guarded the border, he was promoted to Defense Commissioner of his home prefecture and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde he came to court and, for his long border service, was promoted to defense commissioner of his prefecture and sent back.

sentences.zh: 自承美內屬，給奉同蕃官例，至是，特詔月增五萬。

translations.literal: Since Chengmei submitted inward, his stipend followed the tribal-official precedent; at this time a special edict added fifty thousand per month.
translations.idiomatic: Since his submission his pay had followed the tribal-officer scale; now an edict specially added fifty thousand per month.

sentences.zh: 尋請於州城置孔子廟，詔可之。

translations.literal: Soon he requested that a Confucius temple be established in the prefectural city; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to build a Confucius temple in the prefectural city, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾被疾，遣中使挾醫視之。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill; palace envoys were sent bringing physicians to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and the court sent envoys with physicians.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，卒，贈恩州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died and was posthumously made Observation Commissioner of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1012 and was posthumously made observation commissioner of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，錄其子文寶、孫懷筠以官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his sons Wenbao and grandson Huaijun were enrolled in office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year his son Wenbao and grandson Huaijun were given offices.

sentences.zh: 初，承美養其長孫文玉為子，奏署殿直，及卒，其本族首領上言文玉曉達軍政，請令襲承美任。

translations.literal: At first Chengmei adopted his eldest grandson Wenyu as son and memorialized appointing him Palace Attendant; when he died, chieftains of his native tribe reported that Wenyu understood military and civil affairs and requested that he inherit Chengmei's post.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmei had adopted his eldest grandson Wenyu and made him a palace attendant; after his death the tribal chiefs petitioned that Wenyu, skilled in military affairs, succeed him.

sentences.zh: 下蕃漢議，議同，以為侍禁、知州事。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down for tribal-and-Han deliberation; the deliberation agreed, and he was made Palace Guard and administrator of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal and Han councils agreed, and he was made a palace guard and acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 文玉父文恭時為侍禁，在沂州，表訴其事，詔改文恭為供奉宮。

translations.literal: Wenyu's father Wengong was then a Palace Guard at Yizhou; he memorialized stating the matter; an edict changed Wengong to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu's father Wengong, a palace guard at Yizhou, petitioned about the matter, and the court made Wengong a palace attendant instead.

sentences.zh: 九年，承美葬，詔以帛緡、米麴、羊酒賜其家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at Chengmei's burial, an edict granted his family silk cash, rice, yeast, sheep, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years later, at Chengmei's funeral, the court granted his family silk, grain, yeast, sheep, and wine.

sentences.zh: 李繼周

translations.literal: Li Jizhou
translations.idiomatic: Li Jizhou

sentences.zh: 李繼周，延州金明人。

translations.literal: Li Jizhou was a native of Jinming in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jizhou was from Jinming in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖計都，父孝順，皆為金明鎮使，繼周嗣掌本族。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jidu and father Xiaoshun were both Jinming garrison commanders; Jizhou succeeded to lead the native clan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jidu and father Xiaoshun had both commanded the Jinming garrison; Jizhou succeeded as head of the clan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，東山蕃落集眾寇清化砦，繼周率眾敗之，殺三千餘人，補殿前承旨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, eastern mountain tribal settlements gathered a host to raid Qinghua Fort; Jizhou led his followers to defeat them, killing more than three thousand, and was made Palace Front Bearer.
translations.idiomatic: In 978 eastern tribes massed against Qinghua fort; Jizhou routed them, killing more than three thousand, and was made a palace front bearer.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，又與侯延廣敗未藏、未腋等族於渾州西山。

translations.literal: During the Yongxi era, together with Hou Yanguang he again defeated the Weicang, Weiye, and other tribes on the western hills of Hunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he and Hou Yanguang defeated the Weicang, Weiye, and other tribes on the western hills of Hunzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，遷殿直，賜介冑、戎器、茶綵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua he was transferred to Palace Attendant and granted armor, military gear, tea, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: In 993 he was made a palace attendant and given armor, weapons, tea, and silks.

sentences.zh: 明年，討李繼遷，命開治塞門、鴉兒兩路，又招降族帳首領二十餘人，率所部入夏州，敗蕃兵數千於石堡砦。

translations.literal: The next year, campaigning against Li Jiqian, he was ordered to open and repair the Saimen and Ya'er routes; he also induced more than twenty tribal tent chieftains to submit, led his command into Xiazhou, and defeated several thousand tribal troops at Shibao Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the campaign against Li Jiqian, he opened the Saimen and Ya'er routes, brought more than twenty tribal chiefs to submit, marched into Xiazhou, and routed several thousand tribal troops at Shibao fort.

sentences.zh: 以功轉供奉官，復加恩賞，仍賜官第。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Palace Attendant, again given favors and rewards, and also granted an official residence.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made a palace attendant, rewarded again, and given an official residence.

sentences.zh: 繼周以阿都關、塞門、盧關等砦最居邊要，遂規修築砦城。

translations.literal: Jizhou, because the forts of Adu Pass, Saimen, and Lumen and others were most strategically placed on the border, then planned to repair and build fort cities.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Adu Pass, Saimen, Lumen, and other forts were the most critical border posts, Jizhou planned to rebuild their walls.

sentences.zh: 在磨盧家、媚咩、拽藏等族居近盧關，未嘗內順。

translations.literal: The Molujia, Meiyang, Zhuaizang, and other tribes dwelling near Lumen Pass had never submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: The Molujia, Meiyang, Zhuaizang, and other tribes near Lumen Pass had never submitted.

sentences.zh: 繼周夜率所部往襲，焚之，斬首俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Jizhou by night led his command to raid them, burned them, and beheaded and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou raided them by night, burned their settlements, and took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，授西京作坊副使，賜袍帶、銀綵、雕戈以寵之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and granted robes, belts, silver silks, and carved halberds to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In 996 he was made deputy commissioner of the western capital workshops and honored with robes, belts, silks, and a carved halberd.

sentences.zh: 大軍討西夏，命為延州路踏白先鋒。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned against Western Xia, he was ordered to be vanguard scout of the Yanzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: In the great campaign against Western Xia he was made scout vanguard of the Yanzhou route.

sentences.zh: 會繼遷邀戰於路，繼周戰卻之。

translations.literal: When Jiqian intercepted and fought on the road, Jizhou fought and repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiqian ambushed him on the march, Jizhou fought him off.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，改西京左藏庫副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was changed to Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he was made deputy commissioner of the western capital left treasury.

sentences.zh: 三年，復為先鋒，人賊境，焚積聚，殺人畜，獲器甲凡六十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the third year he again served as vanguard, entered enemy territory, burned stores, killed people and livestock, and captured armor and weapons totaling more than six hundred thousand items.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he again led the vanguard into enemy country, burned stores, slaughtered people and livestock, and seized more than six hundred thousand pieces of armor and equipment.

sentences.zh: 授供備庫使，領金明縣兵馬都監、新砦解家河盧關路都巡檢。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commissioner of the Supply Reserve and concurrently Jinming County Commander of Troops and Horses, New Fort Xiejiahe-Lumen Pass Route Overall Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner of the supply reserve and overall inspector of Jinming county troops and the Xiejiahe-Lumen pass route.

sentences.zh: 五年，授西京作坊使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he was made commissioner of the western capital workshops.

sentences.zh: 蕃騎入鈔，繼周逐之出境。

translations.literal: Tribal horsemen raided inward; Jizhou drove them beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal horsemen raided, Jizhou drove them back across the border.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，夏人圍麟州，繼周受詔率兵會李繼福掩擊之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde the Xia besieged Linzhou; Jizhou received an edict to lead troops and join Li Jifu in a surprise attack on them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1004 the Xia besieged Linzhou; Jizhou was ordered to join Li Jifu in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 加領誠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was further made to hold the prefecture of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made prefect of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，卒，年六十七，詔邊臣擇其子可襲職者以名聞，邊臣言其子殿直士彬遜愞，從子士用樸忠練邊事，且為部落所伏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, aged sixty-seven; an edict ordered frontier officials to choose which son could inherit the post and report his name; frontier officials said his son Palace Attendant Shibin was mild and compliant, while his nephew Shiyong was plain, loyal, skilled in border affairs, and moreover respected by the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1009 at sixty-seven; the court asked frontier officials to name an heir; they said his son Shibin was mild but his nephew Shiyong was plain, loyal, skilled on the border, and respected by the tribes.

sentences.zh: 乃詔士彬管勾部族事，士用為巡檢都監以左右之。

translations.literal: An edict then made Shibin oversee tribal affairs, with Shiyong as overall inspection superintendent to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The court put Shibin in charge of tribal affairs with Shiyong as inspection superintendent to assist him.

sentences.zh: 士彬後至供備庫副使、金明縣都監、新砦解家河盧關路巡檢。

translations.literal: Shibin later rose to Deputy Commissioner of the Supply Reserve, Jinming County Superintendent, and New Fort Xiejiahe-Lumen Pass Route Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Shibin later became deputy commissioner of the supply reserve, Jinming county superintendent, and inspector of the Xiejiahe-Lumen route.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，元昊反，攻保安軍，而潛兵襲金明，士彬父子俱被禽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding Yuan Hao rebelled, attacked Bao'an Army, and meanwhile sent hidden troops to strike Jinming; Shibin and his son were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: In 1040 Yuan Hao rebelled, attacked Bao'an army, and secretly struck Jinming; Shibin and his son were both captured.

sentences.zh: 士彬兄士紹至內殿崇班，士用至供奉官、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Shibin's elder brother Shishao rose to Inner Palace Honored Class; Shiyong rose to Palace Attendant and Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shibin's brother Shishao became an inner-palace honored-class officer; Shiyong became a palace attendant and gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 李繼福者，亦與繼周同時歸順，授永平砦茭村軍主，以戰功歷歸德將軍，領順州刺史，至內殿崇班、新歸明諸族都巡檢。

translations.literal: Li Jifu also submitted at the same time as Jizhou, was appointed Yongping Fort Jiaocun Army Chief; through battle achievements he rose to Returning Virtue General, held Shunzhou prefect, and reached Inner Palace Honored Class and Overall Inspector of the Newly Submitted Ming Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu, who had submitted with Jizhou, became chief of Jiaocun at Yongping fort, rose through battle to returning-virtue general and prefect of Shunzhou, and eventually became an inner-palace honored-class officer and overall inspector of newly submitted tribes.

sentences.zh: 孫行友

translations.literal: Sun Xingyou
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xingyou

sentences.zh: 孫行友，莫州清苑人，世業農。

translations.literal: Sun Xingyou, a native of Qingyuan in Mozhou, farmed for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xingyou of Qingyuan in Mozhou came from a farming family.

sentences.zh: 初，定州西二百里有狼山者，當易州中路，舊有城堡，邊人賴之以避寇。

translations.literal: At first, two hundred li west of Dingzhou was Wolf Mountain, on the middle route of Yizhou; there was an old fortress on which frontier people relied to escape raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li west of Dingzhou stood Wolf Mountain on the main Yizhou route; an old fort there had long sheltered frontier people from raiders.

sentences.zh: 山中蘭若有尼，姓孫氏，名深意，有術惑眾。

translations.literal: In the mountain orchid temple there was a nun surnamed Sun, named Shenyi, who possessed arts that deluded the masses.
translations.idiomatic: At a mountain temple there lived a nun surnamed Sun, called Shenyi, whose occult arts beguiled the crowd.

sentences.zh: 行友兄子方諫名之為姑帥，事之甚謹。

translations.literal: Xingyou's elder brother's son Fang Jian called her Aunt Commander and served her very carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyou's nephew Fang Jian called her "Aunt Commander" and waited on her with great devotion.

sentences.zh: 及尼坐亡，行友益神其事，因以其術然香燈，聚民漸眾。

translations.literal: When the nun died seated, Xingyou revered the affair all the more; using her arts he lit incense lamps, gathered people, and the crowd gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: When the nun died in meditation, Xingyou treated the matter as even more miraculous; he adopted her rites, lit incense lamps, and drew a steadily growing following.

sentences.zh: 自晉少帝與契丹絕好，邊州困於轉輸，逋民往往依方諫，推以為帥。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Shao of Jin broke good relations with the Khitan, border prefectures were distressed by transport; absconding people often attached themselves to Fang Jian and made him commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shao of Jin broke with the Khitan, border prefectures were strained by supply runs, and refugees often rallied to Fang Jian and chose him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 方諫懼主帥捕逐，乃表歸朝，因署為東北面招收指揮使，且賜院額曰「勝福」。

translations.literal: Fang Jian feared the chief commander would capture and drive him out, so he memorialized submission to the court; he was then appointed Northeast Reception Commanding Envoy, and the abbey plaque "Shengfu" was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing pursuit by the local commander, Fang Jian submitted to the court and was made northeast reception commanding envoy; the abbey was granted the name Shengfu.

sentences.zh: 每契丹軍來，必率其徒襲擊之，鎧仗、畜產所得漸多，人益依以避難焉。

translations.literal: Whenever Khitan armies came, he invariably led his followers to strike them; armor, weapons, and livestock taken gradually increased, and people relied on him all the more to escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Khitan forces appeared, he led his men against them; booty in arms and livestock grew, and more people looked to him for refuge.

sentences.zh: 易、定帥聞於朝，因以方諫為邊界遊奕使，行友副之。

translations.literal: The commanders of Yi and Ding reported to court, and Fang Jian was made Border Patrol Commissioner, with Xingyou as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi and Ding commanders reported to court, which appointed Fang Jian border patrol commissioner with Xingyou as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 自是捍禦侵軼，多所殺獲。

translations.literal: From then on they defended against incursions and raids, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they repelled incursions and took many kills and captives.

sentences.zh: 乘勝入祁溝關、平庸城，破飛狐砦，契丹頗畏之，邊民千餘家賴以無患。

translations.literal: Pressing victory, they entered Qigou Pass and Pingyong City, captured Feihu Fort; the Khitan greatly feared them, and more than a thousand frontier households relied on them to be free of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed their advantage into Qigou Pass and Pingyong City, took Feihu Fort, and so daunted the Khitan that more than a thousand frontier households lived secure under their protection.

sentences.zh: 然亦陰持兩端，以圖自固。

translations.literal: Yet they also secretly kept to both sides to strengthen themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they also hedged between rival powers to secure their own position.

sentences.zh: 已而晉師失律，薊人道契丹陷中原，方諫之密構也。

translations.literal: Before long the Jin army lost discipline; people of Ji said the Khitan's conquest of the Central Plains was Fang Jian's secret plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Jin armies collapsed; people of Ji blamed the Khitan conquest of the Central Plains on Fang Jian's secret collusion.

sentences.zh: 契丹授方諫定州節度，行友易州刺史。

translations.literal: The Khitan made Fang Jian military commissioner of Dingzhou and Xingyou prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan made Fang Jian military commissioner of Dingzhou and Xingyou prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以蕃將耶律忠代方諫於雲州，方諫不受命，歸保狼山。

translations.literal: Soon the tribal general Yelü Zhong replaced Fang Jian at Yunzhou; Fang Jian refused the appointment and returned to hold Wolf Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitan general Yelü Zhong was sent to replace Fang Jian at Yunzhou; Fang Jian refused and withdrew to Wolf Mountain.

sentences.zh: 契丹北歸，焚劫山中，方諫自狼山率眾復保定州，歸命於漢，授行友易州刺史，行義泰州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Khitan withdrew north, they burned and plundered the mountains; Fang Jian from Wolf Mountain led the masses to recover and hold Dingzhou, submitted to Han, and Xingyou was appointed prefect of Yizhou and Xingyi prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan withdrew north they burned the mountains; Fang Jian marched from Wolf Mountain, retook Dingzhou, and submitted to Han; Xingyou was made prefect of Yizhou and Xingyi prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 弟兄掎角以居，寇每入，諸軍鎮閉壘坐視，一無所得。

translations.literal: The brothers lived in mutual support like horns of a beast; whenever raiders entered, the garrison towns closed their forts and watched; nothing was gained.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers held adjoining positions in mutual support; whenever raiders came, the frontier garrisons shut their walls and watched from afar without intercepting a single prize.

sentences.zh: 行友嘗遣都校王友遇巡警於石河，與契丹遇，殺百餘騎，又嘗獲其刺史蔡幅順、清苑令王璉。

translations.literal: Xingyou once sent Commander Wang Youyu to patrol at Shihe; encountering Khitan, he killed more than a hundred horsemen; he also once captured their prefect Cai Fushun and Qingyuan magistrate Wang Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyou once sent Commander Wang Youyu to patrol the Shi River, where he killed more than a hundred Khitan horsemen; he also captured the Khitan prefect Cai Fushun and Qingyuan magistrate Wang Lian.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，契丹復犯塞，行友禦之，俘殺數百人。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era the Khitan again violated the frontier; Xingyou defended and captive-killed several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou the Khitan again raided the frontier; Xingyou fought them off and killed or captured several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 周太祖北征，行友道獻俘馘人馬以求見，且請自效，廼厚加賜予，留之軍門。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou marched north, Xingyou on the road presented captives and severed heads, men and horses, seeking an audience and asking to serve; he was richly rewarded and kept at army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizu of Zhou's northern campaign, Xingyou met the army with captives and severed heads, asked for an audience, and offered his service; the emperor richly rewarded him and kept him at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及周祖受命，行友屢上言偵得契丹離合，願得勁兵三千，乘間平定幽州，乃移方諫鎮華州，以行友為定州留後。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu received the Mandate, Xingyou repeatedly memorialized that he had spied out Khitan divisions and unions, wished to have three thousand crack troops, and seize the opportunity to pacify Youzhou; Fang Jian was then moved to garrison Huazhou and Xingyou made acting governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Taizu took the throne, Xingyou repeatedly reported Khitan disunity and asked for three thousand elite troops to seize Youzhou; Fang Jian was transferred to Huazhou and Xingyou made acting governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，正授節鉞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was formally invested with the command seal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande he received full military commission.

sentences.zh: 世宗自河東還，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong returned from Hedong, he was made Honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong returned from Hedong, Xingyou was made honorary grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 六年，世宗北征，行友攻下契丹之易州，擒其刺史任欽以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Emperor Shizong marched north; Xingyou attacked and took Yizhou from the Khitan and presented its captured prefect Ren Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xiande, during Emperor Shizong's northern campaign, Xingyou took Yizhou from the Khitan and presented the captured prefect Ren Qin.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made associate director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 狼山佛舍妖妄愈甚，眾趨之不可禁，行友不自安，累表乞解官歸山，詔不允。

translations.literal: The Buddhist abode at Wolf Mountain grew ever more extravagantly deluded; the crowd flocked to it and could not be forbidden; Xingyou was ill at ease, repeatedly memorialized asking to resign office and return to the mountain; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wolf Mountain temple grew ever more febrile with cult activity; crowds flocked there beyond restraint; uneasy, Xingyou repeatedly asked to resign and retire to the hills, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，乃徙其帑廩，召集丁壯，繕治兵甲，欲還狼山以自固。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he moved his treasury stores, gathered strong youths, repaired armor and weapons, and wished to return to Wolf Mountain to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: In 961 he moved his stores, mustered fighting men, and readied arms, intending to withdraw to Wolf Mountain and fortify himself there.

sentences.zh: 兵馬都監藥繼能密表其事，太祖遣閣門副使武懷節馳騎會鎮、趙之兵，稱巡邊，直入其城，行友不之覺。

translations.literal: Commander of Troops and Horses Yao Jineng secretly memorialized the matter; Emperor Taizu sent Vice Commissioner of the Inner Gate Wu Huaijie riding at speed to join the troops of Zhen and Zhao, claiming a border inspection, and entered the city directly; Xingyou did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Troop commander Yao Jineng reported secretly; Emperor Taizu sent Vice Commissioner Wu Huaijie at speed with forces from Zhen and Zhao, ostensibly on a border tour, straight into the city before Xingyou knew.

sentences.zh: 既而出詔示之，令舉族赴闕，行友蒼黃聽命。
