translations.literal: Then an edict was shown him, ordering the whole clan to come to court; Xingyou in alarm obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then produced ordering his entire clan to the capital; Xingyou, taken aback, obeyed.

sentences.zh: 既至，命侍御史李維岳就第鞫之，得實，下詔切責，削奪從前官爵。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, Censor Li Weiyue was ordered to examine him at his residence; the facts were established, a severe edict of rebuke was issued, and his previous offices and ranks were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, Censor Li Weiyue tried him at his residence; the charges were proved, a stern edict rebuked him, and his former ranks were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 勒歸私第。

translations.literal: He was compelled to return to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered confined to his private residence.

sentences.zh: 仍戮其部下數人，遣使馳詣狼山，輦其尼師之屍焚之。

translations.literal: Several of his subordinates were still executed; envoys were dispatched at speed to Wolf Mountain to cart the nun-master's corpse and burn it.
translations.idiomatic: Several of his followers were executed, and messengers were sent posthaste to Wolf Mountain to bring out the dead nun's body and burn it.

sentences.zh: 行友弟易州刺史方進、兄子保塞軍使全暉皆詣闕待罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: Xingyou's younger brother Yizhou Prefect Fangjin and elder brother's son Baosai Army Commissioner Quanhui all came to court to await punishment; an edict released them.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyou's brother Fangjin, prefect of Yizhou, and his nephew Quanhui, commissioner of Baosai army, came to court to answer for the affair and were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，詔免行友禁錮。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year an edict lifted Xingyou's confinement.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn an edict lifted Xingyou's house arrest.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以郊祀恩，起為右龍武軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before long, through the grace of the suburban sacrifice, he was restored as General of the Right Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, by the grace of the suburban sacrifice, he was restored as general of the Right Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，遷右監門衛大將軍，又改左龍武軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he was moved to Grand General of the Right Gate Guard Corps, then changed to Grand General of the Left Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 964 he became grand general of the Right Gate Guard corps, then grand general of the Left Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，卒，年八十，贈左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he died, aged eighty; he was posthumously made Senior General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 981 at eighty and was posthumously made senior general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 方進至德州刺史。

translations.literal: Fangjin rose to Prefect of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fangjin rose to become prefect of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 子全照。

translations.literal: Son: Quanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Quanzhao.

sentences.zh: 子 全照

translations.literal: Son: Quanzhao
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao

sentences.zh: 全照，字繼明，以蔭補殿直，雍熙中授京南巡檢，俄隸幽州部署曹彬麾下，遷供奉官、閣門祗候歷靜戎、威虜二軍監軍。

translations.literal: Quanzhao, courtesy name Jiming, entered by hereditary privilege as Palace Attendant; in Yongxi he was made Capital South Inspector; soon he served under Youzhou Deployment Commissioner Cao Bin, was promoted to Palace Attendant, Gate Commissioner, and successively supervised the Jingrong and Weilu armies.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao, courtesy name Jiming, entered service by privilege as a palace attendant; in Yongxi he became capital-south inspector, soon joined Cao Bin's Youzhou command, and rose to palace attendant and gate commissioner, supervising the Jingrong and Weilu armies in turn.

sentences.zh: 從田重進擊賊有功，就加西京作坊使，兼知威虜軍，連為廣韶、鄜延二路都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Following Tian Chongjin in attacking bandits he had merit; he was then made Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and concurrently knew Weilu Army; he successively served as Overall Inspector of the Guang-Shao and Fu-Yan routes.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Tian Chongjin against rebels, he earned merit and was made commissioner of the western capital workshops while commanding Weilu army; he then served in turn as overall inspector on the Guang-Shao and Fu-Yan routes.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，率兵與李繼隆克綏州，因與張崇貴等同戍守之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua he led troops with Li Jilong to take Suizhou, and together with Zhang Chonggui and others garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: In 994 he joined Li Jilong in taking Suizhou and garrisoned it with Zhang Chonggui and others.

sentences.zh: 俄護屯兵於夏州，兼知州事。

translations.literal: Soon he protected stationed troops at Xizhou and concurrently handled prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He soon guarded troops at Xizhou and also administered the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召還，為登萊路都巡檢使，遷左藏庫使、延州監軍兼阿都關盧關路都巡檢事。

translations.literal: Recalled, he was made Overall Inspector of the Deng-Lai route; he was moved to Commissioner of the Left Treasury, Yanzhou Military Supervisor, and concurrently Overall Inspector of the Adu Pass-Lumen Pass route.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he became overall inspector of the Deng-Lai route, then commissioner of the left treasury, Yanzhou military supervisor, and overall inspector of the Adu and Lumen passes.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，人掌軍頭引見司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he entered to manage the Army Presentation Introduction Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he took charge of the army presentation office.

sentences.zh: 二年，加如京使，為涇原路鈐轄兼安撫都監，是冬徙幷、汾等州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made Envoy Bearing Credentials and served as Tongzhuan of the Jingyuan route and concurrently Pacification Superintendent; that winter he was moved to Overall Inspector of Bing, Fen, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became envoy bearing credentials, Jingyuan route tongzhuan and pacification superintendent; that winter he was made overall inspector of Bing, Fen, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 三年，改知順安軍，代還，復為環慶路鈐轄，與李繼和規度靈州道路。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to know Shun'an Army; when replaced and returned, he again became Tongzhuan of the Huanqing route and with Li Jihe surveyed the roads to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was put in charge of Shun'an army; after his replacement he returned as Huanqing route tongzhuan and with Li Jihe surveyed routes to Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，加西上閣門使，復為環慶路鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Western Upper Inner Gate Commissioner and again became Tongzhuan of the Huanqing route.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he became western upper inner-gate commissioner and again served as Huanqing route tongzhuan.

sentences.zh: 五年，將城綏州，以慕興為綏州路部署，全照為鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year they were about to fortify Suizhou; Mu Xing was made Suizhou Route Deployment Commissioner and Quanzhao Tongzhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later, as the court prepared to rebuild Suizhou, Mu Xing was made route deployment commissioner and Quanzhao tongzhuan.

sentences.zh: 既又慮全照素剛執，與興不協，乃以曹璨代之。

translations.literal: Then they also feared Quanzhao was by nature stubborn and would not harmonize with Xing, so Cao Can replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Concerned that Quanzhao's stubborn temperament would clash with Mu Xing, the court replaced him with Cao Can.

sentences.zh: 既調兵夫二萬餘，全照言其非便，乃罷。

translations.literal: After more than twenty thousand labor conscripts had been mobilized, Quanzhao said it was inexpedient, and the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty thousand laborers had been mobilized, Quanzhao argued the plan was impracticable and it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又嘗命度地河北，全照言沿河高阜可分置城堡屯戍者，寧邊軍南、武強縣側凡二處，上重於興役，止命營安平南，徙置祁州。

translations.literal: He was also once ordered to survey land north of the Yellow River; Quanzhao said along the river's high mounds two places could be separately set with castles for garrison—south of Ningbian Army and beside Wuqiang County; the emperor was reluctant to impose heavy labor and only ordered a camp south of Anping and the relocation of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to survey Hebei, Quanzhao proposed two high riverbank sites near Ningbian army and Wuqiang county for fortified garrisons; the emperor, wary of the labor burden, approved only a camp south of Anping and moved Qizhou there.

sentences.zh: 俄知天雄軍府。

translations.literal: Soon he knew the Tianxiong Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became administrator of Tianxiong army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，上裁定防秋禦戎之要，命為寧邊軍部署，領兵八千扼要害之路。

translations.literal: In the sixth year summer the emperor settled the essentials of autumn defense against barbarians and ordered him deployed at Ningbian Army, leading eight thousand troops to block the critical pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the emperor finalized autumn frontier defense and made Quanzhao deployment commissioner at Ningbian army with eight thousand men to hold the key approach.

sentences.zh: 以全照好陵人，取其嘗所保薦者王德鈞、裴自榮共事焉。

translations.literal: Because Quanzhao liked to domineer over others, those he had once recommended—Wang Dejun and Pei Zirong—were taken to serve with him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Quanzhao tended to bully subordinates, the court paired him with two men he had once recommended—Wang Dejun and Pei Zirong.

sentences.zh: 全照形短精悍，知兵，以嚴毅整眾，然性剛使氣，專任刑罰。

translations.literal: Quanzhao was short in stature, keen and hardy, knew warfare, disciplined the masses with stern severity, yet by nature was obstinate and hot-tempered, relying solely on punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao was short, wiry, and skilled in war; he kept his troops in order through stern discipline, but his stubborn, combative temperament made him lean heavily on punishment.

sentences.zh: 中書初進擬嚴州刺史，上曰：「全照深刻，常慮人以嚴察議己，今授此州，似涉譏誚。

translations.literal: The Secretariat at first proposed him for Prefect of Yanzhou; the emperor said: "Quanzhao is harsh and penetrating; he always fears people will discuss him as stern and scrutinizing; now to grant this prefecture seems to touch on ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat first proposed him for prefect of Yanzhou, the emperor said, "Quanzhao is harsh by nature and always worried that people would mock his severity; giving him Yanzhou would look like a taunt.

sentences.zh: 」乃改焉。

translations.literal: " So it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: " So the appointment was changed.

sentences.zh: 三年，為邠寧環慶都部署。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Overall Deployment Commissioner of Binning-Huanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he became overall deployment commissioner of Binning and Huanqing.

sentences.zh: 趙德明納款，朝議減西鄙戍兵，令屯近地，全照以邊防不可無備，未即奉詔。

translations.literal: Zhao Deming submitted allegiance; court discussion proposed reducing western frontier garrison troops and ordering them stationed near; Quanzhao held the frontier defense could not go unprovided and did not immediately obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Deming submitted, the court debated thinning western garrisons and moving troops inland; Quanzhao argued the frontier could not be left undefended and did not obey at once.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「全照是好勇多言者。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Quanzhao is one who loves bravery and speaks much.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Quanzhao is bold and talkative.

sentences.zh: 德明使已至闕，復何慮焉？

translations.literal: Deming's envoy has already reached court; what is there again to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Deming's envoy is already at court—what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 」因徙全照知永興軍府，仍拜四方館使。

translations.literal: " He then moved Quanzhao to know Yongxing Army headquarters and still made him Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He transferred Quanzhao to Yongxing army headquarters and made him commissioner of the Four Directions Hall.

sentences.zh: 西師移屯者至府，命全照兼駐泊鈐轄。

translations.literal: Western army troops being relocated arrived at the headquarters; Quanzhao was ordered concurrently to serve as Stationed Garrison Tongzhuan.
translations.idiomatic: When relocated western troops reached the prefecture, Quanzhao was made their stationed garrison tongzhuan as well.

sentences.zh: 全照許州有別墅，求典是州，可之。

translations.literal: Quanzhao had a separate villa in Xuzhou; he requested to administer that prefecture, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao owned a villa in Xuzhou and asked to govern that prefecture; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，遷引進使。

translations.literal: In Dazhong Xiangfu he was moved to Introducing Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhong Xiangfu he was made introducing envoy.

sentences.zh: 逾歲表求歸朝，命掌閣門、客省、四方館事。

translations.literal: After a year he memorialized asking to return to court; he was ordered to manage Inner Gate, Guest Reception, and Four Directions Hall affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he asked to return to court and was put in charge of the inner gate, guest reception, and Four Directions Hall.

sentences.zh: 四年，車駕西幸，留為新城都巡檢，未幾，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year when the imperial carriage traveled west, he was left as Overall Inspector of Xincheng; before long he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the emperor traveled west, he was left as overall inspector of Xincheng; he died soon after, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 論曰：五代之季，邊圉之不靖也久矣。

translations.literal: Discussion: At the end of the Five Dynasties, the borders' unrest had long endured.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: By the close of the Five Dynasties, the frontier had been unsettled for a long time.

sentences.zh: 太祖之興，雖不勤遠略，而向之陸梁跋扈而不可制者，莫不竭忠效節，雖奔走僵仆而不避，豈人心之有異哉？

translations.literal: At the rise of Emperor Taizu, though he did not labor at distant strategy, those who formerly had been unruly, overbearing, and uncontrollable all exhausted loyalty and offered their devotion; though they ran till they collapsed they did not avoid it—was human hearts' difference the reason?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu rose, though he did not pursue grand distant campaigns, even the once unruly and uncontrollable border lords poured out loyalty and served to exhaustion—had human nature somehow changed?

sentences.zh: 良由威德之並用，控御之有道也。

translations.literal: Truly it was because awe and virtue were jointly employed and control had its method.
translations.idiomatic: No—it was because he wielded both awe and kindness, and governed the frontier with skill.

sentences.zh: 折氏據有府谷，與李彜興之居夏州，初無以異。

translations.literal: The Zhe clan held Fugu, and Li Yixing dwelt at Xizhou—at first there was no difference.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhe clan held Fugu much as Li Yixing held Xizhou; at first the two cases were hardly different.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其嚮化，許以世襲，雖不無世卿之嫌，自從阮而下，繼生名將，世篤忠貞，足為西北之捍，可謂無負於宋者矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu praised their turning toward civilization and permitted hereditary succession; though not without the suspicion of hereditary ministers, from Congruan downward successive generations produced famed generals, generations deeply loyal and true, sufficient as northwest bulwarks—one may say they did not fail Song.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu rewarded their submission with hereditary office; though that smacked of feudal privilege, from Congruan onward the family produced one loyal frontier commander after another and became the northwest bulwark—the Zhe did not fail the Song.

sentences.zh: 承美、繼周，分蒞種落，亦能世其職者也。

translations.literal: Chengmei and Jizhou separately presided over tribal settlements and likewise could inherit their offices through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmei and Jizhou likewise held tribal commands in succession across generations.

sentences.zh: 繼業雖出賊叛之族，而有循良之風。

translations.literal: Jiye though from a bandit-rebel clan had the air of steady goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye came from a rebellious house yet governed with steady, humane discipline.

sentences.zh: 方諫、行友介遼、晉間，持兩端以取將相，終以首鼠獲咎，其諸異端之害歟？

translations.literal: Fang Jian and Xingyou stood between Liao and Jin, kept to both ends to obtain general and chancellor posts, and in the end were blamed as fence-sitters—is this the harm of various heterodoxies?
translations.idiomatic: Fang Jian and Xingyou, straddling Liao and Jin, played both sides to win high office and in the end paid for their vacillation—is this the cost of border cults and double-dealing?

sentences.zh: 全照職親禁衛，素稱嚴果，而昧於弭兵之利，君子所不予也。

translations.literal: Quanzhao's office was close to the palace guard; he was known for sternness and resolution, yet was blind to the benefit of quelling war—what gentlemen do not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhao held a palace guard post and was known for stern efficiency, yet he failed to see the value of easing military tensions—a failing no gentleman would condone.
